agree.reason: A four-chair owner who pays her cousin $600 a year sees $199 a month (about $2,388 a year) and nothing telling her she can keep him for her taxes, so she probably won't book the call.

honest.reason: The figures match the brief and the 9-of-12 close record is stated plainly, but 'most bookkeepers have to learn how salons work on your dime' and 'paid correctly and on time' are claims the brief doesn't support.

works_the_facts.reason: It repeats the numbers without working them: it never says that 9 of 31 clients, nearly a third, paid their accountant less, never calls 29 of 31 a 94% retention rate with no client leaving unhappy, and never sets the $800 saving against the yearly cost.

right_comparison.reason: The reader's actual alternative is a once-a-year tax-time bookkeeper for $600, but the page compares itself only to vague 'most bookkeepers' and 'account teams' that she doesn't use.

qualification.reason: The 10th-of-the-month target and the accountant-savings hedge have no consequence attached, even though a free month for any missed close and 30-day no-contract cancellation were available and are exactly the checkable commitments needed.

objections.reason: Her main objections, price against the $600 and loyalty to her cousin, are never met, though 'I don't do income tax returns, your own preparer keeps doing them' would have handled both, and the bare 'no phone Sundays or Mondays' line raises a worry without saying calls run Tuesday to Saturday.

fit.reason: It is about 350 words of sales-page copy with clear sections and ends in a booking button, as the brief asked.
